kilauea_notices.title: HAWAIIAN VOLCANO OBSERVATORY DAILY UPDATE
kilauea_notices.message: HVO Kilauea ORANGE/WATCH - Intermittent lava flows have continued from the north vent over the past day. High fountaining remains a possibility today or anytime within the next few days.
kilauea_notices.detail: Overview: Lava flows have occurred intermittently over the past day from the north vent. Summit inflation that continued through most of yesterday shifted to deflation around 3 a.m. this morning. Seismic tremor at the summit is elevated with fluctuations in tremor associated with the beginning and end of lava overflows. SO2 emission rates are elevated. Episode 56 high fountaining remains a possibility today or anytime through November 8 based upon prior behavior once precursory flows have begun. Summit Observations: Intermittent overflows continued from the north vent over the past day. Overflows were typically around 15-20 minutes in duration, and this morning 2-3 per hour were occurring. Strong glow could be seen from the southwest vent overnight, along with occasional spatter and flames. Background seismic tremor began increasing around 6 a.m. and remains elevated as of this morning. Periodic strong tremor bursts associated with the vigorous drain back of lava marking the end of each overflow picked up this morning. Six small earthquakes were located at the summit in the past day, with most beneath the south caldera region. This morning the Uēkahuna tiltmeter (UWD) had recovered a total of 17.6 microradians of tilt since the end of episode 55. Inflationary tilt that continued through yesterday and early this morning switched to deflationary tilt around 3 a.m., with deflationary tilt continuing this morning. Sulfur dioxide (SO2) emission rates averaged 4000 tonnes per day (t/d) after overflows began on November 2. Strong trade winds this morning are carrying volcanic gases southwest toward Kaʻū. Rift Zone Observations: Rates of seismicity and ground deformation remain low in the East Rift Zone and Southwest Rift Zone. SO2 emissions from the East Rift Zone remain below the detection limit. Analysis: Following episode 55 on October 17, 2026, summit tiltmeters initially recorded a typical post-fountaining recovery, with a steady upward trend that gradually slowed and was interrupted by several small fluctuations. This inflationary trend was interrupted by deflation on November 2, with fluctuating tilt since that time. Inflation based models are probably not reliable unless steady inflationary tilt returns to the summit. The onset of precursory overflows typically indicates that a new episode of fountaining is within 1-6 days. It is reasonable to estimate that the onset of episode 56 fountaining will occur between now and November 8, provided conditions remain stable at the summit. Kīlauea has been erupting episodically since December 23, 2024, from two primary vents (north and south) within Halemaʻumaʻu at the summit. Lava fountaining episodes generally last less than 12 hours and are separated by pauses of two or more weeks. HVO continues to closely monitor Kīlauea and remains in contact with Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park and the Hawaiʻi County Civil Defense Agency regarding eruptive hazards. Summary of episode 55: A detailed account of episode 55 is given in the HVO Daily Update for October 17: https://volcanoes.usgs.gov/hans-public/notice/DOI-USGS-HVO-2026-10-17T15:47:29+00:00 Episode 55 of the ongoing Halemaʻumaʻu eruption began at 3:19 a.m. HST on October 17 and ended abruptly at 9:03 a.m. HST on the same day. The maximum lava fountain height was approximately 720 feet (220 meters) above ground level from the north vent. The south and west vents never fountained during this episode but did produce overflows prior to the fountaining episode. The maximum plume height was approximately 25,000 (7,500 meters) above mean sea level. Tephra fall was restricted mostly to the closed area of Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park, southwest of the active Halemaʻumaʻu vents. Hazards: Eruptive activity since December 2024 has been occurring within a closed area of Hawai'i Volcanoes National Park. mauna_loa_notices.title: HAWAIIAN VOLCANO OBSERVATORY MONTHLY UPDATE
mauna_loa_notices.message: HVO Mauna Loa GREEN/NORMAL - Mauna Loa earthquake counts decreased in September compared to August, and minor inflation continues.
mauna_loa_notices.detail: Mauna Loa had a decrease in seismic activity compared to the previous month; a total of 53 earthquakes were detected in Mauna Loa's summit region during the September reporting period, after 87 in August. Most earthquakes occurred deep beneath the upper Southwest Rift Zone or broadly scattered around the upper flanks. No earthquakes occurred directly beneath Mokuʻāweoweo. Data from Global Positioning System (GPS) instruments on Mauna Loa showed slight inflation across the summit region in the past month. Oscillations between contraction and inflation patterns during non-eruptive periods are normal, but inflation has been the dominant trend since the 2022 eruption, consistent with magma refilling the summit reservoir system. Gas and temperature data from a station on Mauna Loa's Southwest Rift Zone indicate these values are at background levels, with little change relative to previous months. HVO continues to closely monitor Mauna Loa and will issue another update in one month, or earlier, should conditions change significantly.
